step: 3rd stage: tokenize the rebuilt group_size=1 dataset and enter it in the ledger

ledger.build_scripts: data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/build-scripts/ - the six scripts that made the split directories, the manifest, the measurements and this report. They are under data/, which is gitignored, because this stage was not allowed to add to tools/. build_manifest.py should be promoted to tools/ with a test; until it is, the manifest cannot be rebuilt from the repository alone.

order: 1. audio  (before text: prepare_dataset trims or pads the text stream to the audio length, so audio is the authority)
4. record the text flags in the manifest sidecar
5. record and verify the provenance of inputs and outputs

tokenize_audio.train: OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project --with "torch==2.4.1" --with "torchaudio==2.4.1" --with moshi==0.1.0 --with numpy --with soundfile --with huggingface_hub --with tqdm python -m tools.tokenize_audio --audio_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/audio --output_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/tok-audio --audio_tokenizer_repo kyutai/moshiko-pytorch-bf16 --audio_tokenizer_name tokenizer-e351c8d8-checkpoint125.safetensors --audio_chunk_size 1200 --device cpu --num_workers 1
tokenize_audio.dev: OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project --with "torch==2.4.1" --with "torchaudio==2.4.1" --with moshi==0.1.0 --with numpy --with soundfile --with huggingface_hub --with tqdm python -m tools.tokenize_audio --audio_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/audio --output_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/tok-audio --audio_tokenizer_repo kyutai/moshiko-pytorch-bf16 --audio_tokenizer_name tokenizer-e351c8d8-checkpoint125.safetensors --audio_chunk_size 1200 --device cpu --num_workers 1

tokenize_text.train: OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project --with numpy --with sentencepiece --with huggingface_hub --with tqdm python -m tools.tokenize_text --word_transcript_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/text --output_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/tok-text --text_tokenizer_repo nu-dialogue/j-moshi-ext --text_tokenizer_name tokenizer_spm_32k_3.model --no_whitespace_before_word --text_padding_id 3 --end_of_text_padding_id 0 --audio_tokenizer_frame_rate 12.5 --num_workers 1
tokenize_text.dev: OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project --with numpy --with sentencepiece --with huggingface_hub --with tqdm python -m tools.tokenize_text --word_transcript_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/text --output_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/tok-text --text_tokenizer_repo nu-dialogue/j-moshi-ext --text_tokenizer_name tokenizer_spm_32k_3.model --no_whitespace_before_word --text_padding_id 3 --end_of_text_padding_id 0 --audio_tokenizer_frame_rate 12.5 --num_workers 1

prepare_dataset.train: OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project --with numpy --with pandas --with pyarrow --with tqdm python -m tools.prepare_dataset --tokenized_text_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/tok-text --tokenized_audio_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/tok-audio --output_prefix data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/parquet/train --text_padding_id 3 --num_examples_per_parquet 100000
prepare_dataset.dev: OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project --with numpy --with pandas --with pyarrow --with tqdm python -m tools.prepare_dataset --tokenized_text_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/tok-text --tokenized_audio_dir data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/tok-audio --output_prefix data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/parquet/dev --text_padding_id 3 --num_examples_per_parquet 100000

commands.record_tokenize: nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -m tools.text_stream_audit record-tokenize --dataset_id v-real-v2 --manifest experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/manifests/v-real-v2.jsonl --out experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/manifests/v-real-v2-tokenize.json --split train --provenance recorded --recorded_at 2026-08-26 -- <the tokenize_text argv above>   # then the same with --split dev --append
commands.provenance_record: nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -m tools.provenance record --out data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/tokenize-provenance.json --artifact-id v-real-v2:tokenized --tool 'tools/tokenize_audio.py + tools/tokenize_text.py + tools/prepare_dataset.py' --captured-at 2026-08-26 --why '...' --input train-audio=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/audio --input train-text=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/text --input dev-audio=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/audio --input dev-text=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/text --output train-tok-audio=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/tok-audio --output train-tok-text=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/train/tok-text --output dev-tok-audio=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/tok-audio --output dev-tok-text=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/dev/tok-text --output parquet=data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/parquet
commands.verify: nice -n 19 uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -m tools.provenance verify --record data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/tokenize-provenance.json --quiet

tokenize_audio.note: Every one of them was passed explicitly anyway except --resume. --device cpu is NOT the default (the default is cuda) and is the flag that matters: mps runs and produces a different parquet from the same wav.

prepare_dataset.note: The basename of --output_prefix is the dialogue_id namespace, so it must stay train / dev; the ids come out as train/v-001 etc., the same namespace M3 used, which is what lets v-real-v1 and v-real-v2 be joined to the same dialogue.

flags.not_recorded_by_the_sidecar: tools/text_stream_audit.py record-tokenize covers tokenize_text.py only. The audio and parquet flags above are recorded here, in this report, and nowhere else. If the sidecar mechanism is extended, extend it to those two tools.

environment.why_thread_limited: the user asked that this machine not be loaded; measured below to make no difference to the tokens

inputs.how_the_split_directories_were_made: group_size=1, so each training row is exactly one dialogue. data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/<split>/{audio,text} was materialised by copying each row out of data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/v-real/sequences/<split>/ under the dialogue's own name. Every copy was checked against both the sequence file and the dialogue file and against the sha256 the build report recorded: 160 triples, 0 disagreements. Naming them by dialogue is what makes prepare_dataset emit dialogue_id train/v-001 instead of train/train-seq-001.

provenance.verify_result: inputs: match (160 files unchanged) / outputs: match (162 files unchanged), exit 0
provenance.not_covered: the text tokenizer lives in the Hugging Face cache outside the repository root, so tools/provenance.py cannot fingerprint it; its sha256 is in environment.text_tokenizer above

accounting.note: prepare_dataset raises StemMismatchError rather than writing a partial parquet, so equal counts here are not the only thing standing between a missing dialogue and a silently short dataset.

parquet.min_length_flag: omitted, so nothing is dropped by length at training time

text_stream.what_the_counterfactual_proves: The shipped parquet's non-padding counts equal the with_flag pass exactly (train A 1356/2515, B 3271/6069; dev A 162/302, B 367/679) and differ from the without_flag pass at every position. So --no_whitespace_before_word was not merely recorded as true, it is measurable in the artifact. This is the check that would have caught M3 on the day rather than three days later.

decoded_sample.speaker: A
decoded_sample.pieces: <unk>▁また<unk>、東<unk>寺<unk>のように<unk>、五<unk>大<unk>明<unk>王<unk>と呼ばれる<unk>、<unk>主要な<unk>明<unk>王の<unk>中央に<unk>配<unk>される<unk>ことも多い<unk>。
decoded_sample.decoded: また、東寺のように、五大明王と呼ばれる、主要な明王の中央に配されることも多い。

gate_negative_control.what: a parquet tokenized WITHOUT the flag was built from the same tok-audio and placed inside data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/, then the repository gate was run
gate_negative_control.result: tests/test_experiment_assets.py::TextStreamGateTests::test_every_shipped_parquet_is_under_the_gate_or_quarantined FAILED with '0.44640605296343 not less than 0.1 : data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3r/_gate-negative-control/train-001-of-001.parquet speaker A'
gate_negative_control.cleanup: the control parquet was removed; the gate passes again and no parquet outside m3/ and m3r/v-real/parquet/ remains on disk
gate_negative_control.why: a gate that has never been seen to fail is a claim, not a measurement. This one runs at any depth under data/experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama, so it does cover the new dataset's location.

reproducibility.device: cpu, as required. mps is not bit-identical (TOKENIZE_COMMANDS.md section 1: 2 of 21,600 tokens differ, in residual codebooks 4 and 6).

thread_count_probe.why: the run was thread-limited to keep this machine quiet, and a thread count that changed reduction order would change the tokens and quietly void the checksums
thread_count_probe.conclusion: Mimi on cpu is thread-count independent here, and the OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 rerun reproduces the shipped npz byte for byte.

launch_assertions.action_if_different: kill immediately; the dataset is not the one this was computed from

training_shape.matches_m3: M3 ran the same shape - 72 rows, global batch 8, 9 steps per epoch, 45 total - so a difference between the two runs cannot be attributed to the schedule.

length_flags.num_warmup_steps: not set here; it belongs to the training launch
length_flags.note: examples/finetune_accelerate.sh:19-24 sets --max_length 2048 --min_length 128 --num_warmup_steps 500 and M3 omitted all three. At 195-299 frames per row, --max_length 2048 would be a no-op and --min_length 128 would drop nothing, so either choice ships the same 72 rows. Recorded so 4th stage does not have to rediscover it.

held_out.method: text comparison is on NFKC-normalised strings with whitespace and punctuation removed, so a held-out sentence could not hide behind different punctuation. The longest run any dialogue shares with any held-out sentence is 5 characters.

room_tone_caveat.what: 16 of the 117 room-tone segments (1.83 s of 13.25 s) are noise-floor slices taken from 9 corpus DEV recordings; the 10 corpus TEST recordings are excluded by name in roomtone/index.json.
room_tone_caveat.why_it_is_not_held_out_contamination: held-out evaluation uses the test split, which is untouched. The dev slices carry no speech - selection requires RMS in [0.002, 0.01] and voicing below 0.5 - so no dev sentence is learnable from them.
room_tone_caveat.why_it_is_recorded_anyway: registry/v-real-v1.json states that the corpus dev sentences never enter the dataset. That sentence no longer covers the room-tone pool, and a ledger that is true only if nobody reads it carefully is not a ledger.

manifest_validation.what_it_checked: required fields, unique artifact_id, checksum format, that every path resolves inside the data root and its byte_size and sha256 match the file on disk, no COEIROINK provenance, no exact duplicate across splits, no group_id in two splits, and no near-duplicate text across splits.
manifest_validation.what_it_did_not_check: the audio-metadata branch fires only on media_type audio/wav, and every manifest in this repository uses audio/x-wav, so it never runs. The 80 rows' audio blocks were therefore compared directly against tools/experiment_data._audio_metadata: 0 mismatches. A validator that silently skips the rows it was pointed at is the same shape of failure as a flag nobody wrote down.

gates.evidence: utils.data.main_speaker_streams run over every row of both parquets: 9 streams for the main speaker (1 text + 8 audio) plus the other speaker's 8 audio. Counted on the trainer's own function, not asserted from the [9, T] column shape.

gates.gate: bare U+2581 share of emitted text tokens
gates.evidence: tools.text_stream_audit.audit_parquet with the id looked up from the tokenizer (bare_whitespace id 9 = '▁'), not hardcoded. tests/test_experiment_assets.py::TextStreamGateTests measures the same two files.
ceil(72/8) = 9 steps per epoch x 5 epochs

Three independent passes. (1) artifact id: none of the 80 source_artifact_id values is one of the 10 corpus test rows, and all 80 are in the corpus train split. (2) transcript text: the 80 word transcripts that were tokenized share at most a 5-character normalised run with any held-out sentence. (3) the parquet itself: the text stream decoded back through SentencePiece gives the same 5. A renamed or re-derived file would pass (1) and fail (2) and (3).

text_tokens_speaker_A_train.note: identical to M3's with-flag count, because channel A quotes the same 72 corpus sentences

text_tokens_speaker_B_train.note: higher than M3 because speaker B now backchannels inside speaker A's answer

carried_to_the_4th_stage.what: 5 training rows are below the 200-frame floor in m3/DATASET_SPEC.md:110
carried_to_the_4th_stage.why_it_appeared_now: the floor was never breached at the row level while four dialogues were concatenated into one row. group_size=1 exposes it. The same 5 dialogues were under the floor in the withdrawn build too.
carried_to_the_4th_stage.decision_not_taken_here: DATASET_SPEC.md:388 says do not lower the floor, lengthen B's turn. Dropping the 5 rows keeps step 45 (ceil(67/8) x 5 = 45) but changes the split and breaks the pairing with M3. Not this stage's call; nothing was changed.

carried_to_the_4th_stage.what: the acoustic loss weight is effectively 0.99%
carried_to_the_4th_stage.detail: audio_weight = 2x100 + 14x1 = 214, speaker A's acoustic share is 7/214 = 3.27%, and A speaks 30.3% of the time. Measure the breakdown in the 4th stage forward pass before touching it.

the audio and parquet flags live in this report alone. The flag that would hurt most if lost is --device cpu, because mps produces a different parquet from the same wav and nothing downstream notices.
